clue.text: Egg-beater to help rice stirring

definitions.note: slang for a rotary-winged aircraft, from the whirling blades

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of these three words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: use the egg-beater to help when stirring the rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' rearranges TO HELP RICE. 'Egg-beater' looks like a kitchen whisk, but it is old slang for a chopper, whose rotor whirls like a beater.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-beater is informal, mainly American, slang for a rotorcraft, after its spinning blades.

clue.text: Remove a draught in mood of anger

definitions.meaning: in the board game draughts (checkers), to take away an opponent's piece that failed to make a compulsory capture

explanation.surface: Someone shutting out a cold draught while in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; 'draught' looks like a cold breeze, but it is a playing piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In draughts a player forfeits a piece by this penalty for missing a capture; separately the word means a sulk or fit of pique.

clue.text: Jemmy, for instance, turned to get plunder

indicators.note: turned means the word for the jemmy's category is read from end to start

parts.note: a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar, an example of an implement

explanation.surface: A burglar's jemmy is used to get at the plunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses TOOL. A jemmy is the British word for a short crowbar (American 'jimmy').
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder and this word are both synonyms for stolen goods or booty.

clue.text: Six planes appear often in this art form

definitions.text: Six planes appear often in this art form

parts.words: Six planes appear often in this art form
parts.note: a six-faced solid is the cube, and paintings in this movement break subjects into geometric planes and blocks

explanation.surface: An art lover notes that flat aircraft-like shapes recur in a certain style.
explanation.walkthrough: A cube has six plane faces; the early-20th-century movement of Picasso and Braque took its name from its cube-like forms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picasso and Braque movement depicted objects as interlocking geometric facets, named after a six-sided solid.

clue.text: Playing a sly trick like a reck less batsman

definitions.meaning: a careless cricketer hooking a quick delivery to leg

explanation.surface: A careless cricketer who also likes to deceive people.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'reck less' is 'reckless' split across a line. In cricket, to pull is to hit a short ball across to the leg side, and a fast one is a quick delivery, so a rash batsman does exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means cheating someone by a deception; literally a cricketer hitting a quick ball with a pull stroke.

clue.text: Protector of the orb

parts.note: orb here is the eyeball, and the fold of skin that closes over it shields it

explanation.surface: Sounds like a royal guardian of the monarch's jewelled orb.
explanation.walkthrough: The orb looks like the royal regalia, but it is the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin flap that shuts over the eyeball shields it from dust and injury.

clue.text: In the middle of a motorway, driver's first

parts.note: M1 is Britain's first motorway, written with the digit read as the letter I

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the first letter of the word driver

explanation.surface: A driver is stuck in the middle of a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, London to Leeds, is Britain's main motorway; crosswords read its digit 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean surrounded by or among, a preposition of position.

clue.text: Flat at Eton semi-converted

indicators.note: converted means turned into something else, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the English public school, its name used as written

explanation.surface: A flat at Eton, the famous school, has been turned into a semi-detached house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi' looks like part of 'semi-converted', but it is fodder and 'converted' alone rearranges AT ETON SEMI. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat on two floors with its own entrance is this kind of apartment.

clue.text: Free to ring back, having ring back?

definitions.meaning: a telephone line no longer busy, so a caller can phone again
a broken-off engagement, where the betrothal ring has been returned

explanation.surface: Someone told to phone again, who has also had a ring returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a phone line not busy; the second splits the answer as 'dis-' undoing 'engaged', a betrothal undone with the ring handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not occupied, as a phone line, and also no longer betrothed, the ring returned.

clue.text: He hopes to make passes without giving offence

definitions.text: He hopes to make passes without giving offence

parts.words: He hopes to make passes without giving offence
parts.note: the would-be suitor is a soccer player passing the ball without committing a foul

explanation.surface: A shy suitor hopes to make advances without offending anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes' and 'offence' suggest flirting; in soccer a player passes the ball and tries not to foul.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer player aims to pass the ball to teammates and avoid committing fouls.

clue.text: Time-signal from Seville

definitions.meaning: the short beeps the BBC broadcasts on the hour
seeds from Seville oranges, the bitter kind used in marmalade

explanation.surface: A radio time-signal broadcast from the Spanish city of Seville.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC's six short beeps marking the hour are known in Britain by this name; Seville oranges are the bitter marmalade oranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Short broadcast beeps that mark the hour share their name with fruit seeds.

clue.text: Odd fete Sid disrupted in Wales

definitions.text: Odd fete Sid disrupted in Wales

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Sid wrecks a strange Welsh fete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges ODD FETE SID, and the whole clue describes the answer: a Welsh festival, an odd fete to outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh festival of music and poetry competitions is a kind of fete held in Wales.

clue.text: Top dressing applied after stubble is cleared

parts.note: removing bristles from the face with a razor

explanation.surface: Some topsoil is spread once the stubble field has been cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top dressing' and 'stubble' suggest farming, fertiliser on a stubble field, but the top is the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented lotion is dabbed on the face, the body's top, after shaving.

clue.text: Hoping endlessly for an analgesic

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for hoping is dropped

parts.note: hoping means aspiring, longing to achieve something

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops G from ASPIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkiller, acetylsalicylic acid, is an example of a pain-relieving drug.

clue.text: Powder-room of football team

definitions.meaning: a store for gunpowder and weapons
the London soccer club nicknamed the Gunners

explanation.surface: The ladies' room at a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powder-room' looks like a ladies' toilet, but it is a gunpowder store. The London club is named after the Woolwich armoury.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapons and gunpowder store; also the north London soccer club.

clue.text: Love of ear of African flower

parts.note: love means zero, as in tennis scoring
otic is the adjective relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A romantic offers a bloom from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is a river, something that flows: Africa's great river is the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the Nile, the great river that flows through north-east Africa.

clue.text: Rat fit for racing

definitions.meaning: to tell tales to the authorities about someone
of a racehorse, in good condition, written as two words

explanation.surface: A rat fit enough to race.
explanation.walkthrough: As one word it means to tell on someone; split as 'in form' it describes a horse ready to race.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is to betray secrets; also, split, the phrase for an animal in peak racing condition.

clue.text: Abandon pig amid noise

indicators.note: amid means among, so the word for the pig sits inside the word for noise

parts.note: din is a loud noise
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a pig behind amid the racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pig' could suggest HOG, but only the female, a sow, fits inside the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse to acknowledge someone is to abandon them.

clue.text: But did its singers touch the audience?

definitions.text: But did its singers touch the audience?

parts.words: But did its singers touch the audience?
parts.note: to touch someone is slang for asking them for money, and this stage work's characters are mendicants

explanation.surface: A question about whether a performance moved its listeners emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touch' looks like moving people emotionally, but to touch someone for money is to cadge. The 1728 ballad opera by John Gay is about thieves and paupers.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's 1728 ballad opera features rogues and paupers, people who would cadge money.

clue.text: Part of nudism always depressing

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone finds naturism forever gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean gloomy, causing low spirits.

clue.text: Boundaries of motorway in French retirement places

indicators.note: in places the motorway's letters inside the word for French beds

parts.note: lits are beds in French, where one retires for the night
M1 is Britain's first motorway, its digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: The edges of a motorway near French retirement homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement places' suggests old people's homes, but it is beds, where one retires at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean the outer edges or bounds of something.

clue.text: Word of advice to member-walk stealthily!

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint
a member is a part of the body; a toe is one

explanation.surface: Advice to a club member to creep quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a club member, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on the balls of the feet is to move quietly and stealthily.

clue.text: Signs put up by se or in Espana?

definitions.text: Signs put up by se or in Espana?

parts.words: Signs put up by se or in Espana?
parts.note: the printed words are Spanish missing their wavy accent over the n, which a Spaniard would add above it

explanation.surface: A gentleman in Spain posting notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'se or' is señor and Espana is España printed without the wavy mark; a Spaniard would put that mark up over the n.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy diacritic marks placed over a Spanish n are these accents.

clue.text: Very old rock bands from Class II

indicators.note: bands means the letters are regrouped into new bands, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rock bands of great age from a second-tier class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock bands' suggests music, but 'Very old rock' is the definition and 'bands' rearranges CLASS II.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lias is an early Jurassic rock formation, so the adjective describes very ancient strata.

clue.text: French always in battle

parts.note: ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: The French are forever at war.
explanation.walkthrough: AY (or AYE) is a poetic word for ever, always.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight or skirmish is a battle.

clue.text: Right honourable

explanation.surface: The formal title of an MP, Right Honourable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right honourable' looks like the title of a British Privy Counsellor, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means correct or accurate, and also loyal or faithful.

clue.text: Indian farmer said to be in civil commotion

indicators.note: said to be means the word for the commotion is heard, not written

parts.note: a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: An Indian farmer caught up in civil unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' marks a homophone: RIOT sounds like the Indian word for a peasant farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a tenant cultivator or peasant was called by this term.

clue.text: Dry soldier can become so unruly

indicators.note: can become signals that these letters may be turned into something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A sober soldier could turn into a rowdy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can become' rearranges DRY SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean rowdy and hard to control.

clue.text: Sea-bass?

explanation.surface: A fish, the sea bass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-bass' looks like the fish, but splits into two senses: the ocean and a low voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is poetically called this; a bass voice is low-pitched.

clue.text: Chaps on donkeys take time to make judgment

annotationWithheld.why: Chaps on donkeys take time to make judgment (10): ASSES + MEN + T gives nine letters, one S of the answer is supplied by no clue word
annotationWithheld.clue: Chaps on donkeys take time to make judgment
